name: GitHub
effort: About 30 minutes to a working flow.
approval: No review. Organization owners may need to approve your app before it can read org data.
summary: Fastest path in the set. Decide between an OAuth app and a GitHub App first; GitHub recommends GitHub Apps for new integrations.
steps: Open Settings, Developer settings, and create an OAuth App (or a GitHub App).
Set the homepage URL and the authorization callback URL.
Copy the client ID and generate a client secret.
Send users to the authorize endpoint, then exchange the returned code for a token.
blockers: OAuth apps use coarse scopes; fine-grained permissions need a GitHub App.
Organizations that restrict third-party access block your app until an owner approves it.
agentCan: Compare OAuth App versus GitHub App for your use case
Write and test the token exchange against your own account
humanMust: Create the app and secret while signed in
Org owners approve access to organization data
gaps: Rate limits per app type were not reviewed for this guide.

name: Slack
effort: About 1 hour to a working flow in your own workspace. Public listing adds a review period.
approval: Installing in workspaces you control needs no review. Directory listing is reviewed. Workspace admins can restrict installs.
summary: You can run the full OAuth flow right away. Review only matters if you want public directory distribution.
steps: Add HTTPS redirect URLs and bot or user scopes under OAuth and Permissions.
Turn on public distribution so other workspaces can install it.
Send users to the v2 authorize URL and exchange the code at oauth.v2.access.
Optional: submit to the Slack Marketplace with a privacy policy, support contact and scope justification.
blockers: Workspace admins can require approval before members install apps.
Marketplace review timelines and checklist change; confirm current rules before planning.
agentCan: Generate the authorize link and token exchange code
Test in a developer workspace you own
humanMust: Create the app while signed in
gaps: Marketplace review duration is not stated in the pages linked here.

name: Google (Gmail, Drive, Calendar)
effort: Hours to build in testing mode. Production adds verification work and, for restricted scopes, a security assessment.
approval: Sensitive and restricted scopes require verification before the unverified-app warning and user cap go away. No firm turnaround is published.
summary: Easy in testing mode, slow in production. Gmail and broad Drive access are restricted scopes and can require a paid third-party assessment.
steps: Create a Cloud project and configure the OAuth consent screen.
Create a Web application OAuth client with your redirect URIs.
Request only the scopes you need and check whether each is non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted.
Verify domain ownership and publish a homepage and privacy policy.
Submit for verification with scope justifications and a demo video.
If you use restricted scopes, complete the security assessment.
blockers: Apps in testing mode have a test-user cap and short-lived refresh tokens for external users.
Assessment cost and duration for restricted scopes vary by assessor.
agentCan: Choose the narrowest scopes and show their classification
Draft scope justifications and the demo video script
Check your privacy policy against the limited-use rules
humanMust: Own the Cloud project and domain verification
Pay for and complete any security assessment
gaps: Current assessment pricing was not checked.

name: LinkedIn
effort: Hours to create the app. Anything beyond sign-in can take weeks or be declined.
approval: Sign-in products are self-serve. Most data APIs require approval into a partner program.
summary: Creating the app is trivial. Access to useful data is gated by a business review you may not pass.
steps: Create an app at developer.linkedin.com and associate a LinkedIn Company Page.
Request products on the Products tab; sign-in and sharing products are self-serve.
Add redirect URLs and run the three-legged authorization code flow.
Apply to partner programs for any other API and expect questions about your business.
blockers: Many products are limited to approved partners and approval is not assured.
Review criteria and timelines are not published in detail.
Token lifetime and refresh availability differ by program.
agentCan: Tell you which products are self-serve for your use case
Build and test the sign-in flow
humanMust: A Company Page admin must verify the app
Submit and follow up on partner applications
gaps: Partner program eligibility rules were not reviewed in depth.
